what: Two team-seasons selected into Historical V6 were simulated by Candidate 2 during the version-1 runner dry run, outside the formal run.
howItHappened: The dry run's progressive-equivalence section built its evaluator from pkg.m.matchups[0] — the REAL first V6 matchup — rather than from a mock matchup. It played 128 games per surface at the precheck, decision and escalation tiers and recorded per-trait reported states for both sides.
howItWasCaught: the V6 seal's noV6IdInAnySimulationOutput gate. It searches only output-bearing artifacts, so it distinguishes a definition — which is how an unconsumed set exists at all — from a result. It found v6m-1950s in the dry-run artifact and refused the seal.
remedy: Both team-seasons are excluded from the V6 pool with reason SIMULATED_DURING_V6_DRY_RUN, the eligibility and selection policies are re-frozen at version 3.0.0, and the 1950s matchup is re-selected from the remaining eligible teams. The dry run no longer builds its evaluator from a real V6 matchup; it constructs a mock matchup from calibration fixtures.
whyNotWaived: the seal artifact claims Candidate 2 has never been simulated against any of the sixteen selected team-seasons. That claim would have been false for two of them. Weakening the claim to fit what happened would make the seal worthless; excluding the two team-seasons keeps it true.
whatWasNotAffected: no engine behaviour changed, no threshold moved, no Candidate 2 parameter was touched, and the observed states were not used to alter anything. The taint is that the team-seasons are no longer unseen, which is sufficient on its own to disqualify them.
